slides.texte_overlay:
things you should stop
apologising for

taking up space

stop saying sorry for sitting down, asking a question or simply being in a room. you belong there just as much as anyone else, and you don't need permission.

needing help

stop apologising for needing rest, help or time on your own. everyone has needs, and calmly saying yours out loud is healthy and normal, not selfish or weak.

not knowing something

i stopped apologising for what i didn't know and started learning a little every day instead. curiosity feels so much better than constant nervous apologies.
slides.texte_sophia:
not knowing something

i stopped apologising for what i didn't know. now i take one lesson a day in the Sophia app, a bit of history or science, and every day i know a little more than yesterday.

slides.texte_overlay:
changing your mind

stop saying sorry for changing your opinion after learning something new. updating your views isn't weakness, it's proof that you're still learning and growing.

saying no

stop apologising for saying no to things you don't want to do. a kind no protects your time, and the right people will always understand and respect it.
